matches.clause: tighten-only tier binding (tier_binding.py comparing proposed_tier to current Namespace label)
matches.reason: Deleting and recreating a governed Namespace resets tier history, letting a party evade the tighten-only ratchet and re-enter at a looser starting tier without going through the priced loosening pipeline.

The only lawful path to loosen a Namespace's tier is a slow, reviewed manual PR edit, which is incompatible with legitimate time-sensitive needs (pre-approved pentest window / live incident) and chills or forces rule-breaking for beneficial, authorized work.

matches.clause: unlabelled/ungoverned Namespace fails closed to `isolated` (principle 7, 'silence buys nothing')
matches.reason: The blanket fail-closed default punishes benign or beneficial actors (an emergency responder, a harmless test namespace) with the harshest cage regardless of actual risk or intent, chilling legitimate activity.

clause_only.clause: infra declaration / platform role escape from the priced ladder (ADR-0022 'infra is a declaration, not a selection')
clause_only.why_not: A2 attacks the ungoverned granting of the `platform` role itself (a party can self-declare role: platform), while B6 attacks the unrestricted scope of what a legitimate platform-role party may label `infra` (no requirement that the namespace be genuine infrastructure) — different defects in the same clause.

A3 attacks a discovery/coverage gap where a Namespace invisible to the mutating policy's watch is never caged at all, while B2 attacks a documented, working fallthrough where an ungoverned Namespace with a policy-version-claiming pod renders `baseline` — a designed loophole, not a coverage bug.

matches.clause: tighten-only binding check (tier_binding.py) compares proposed_tier only against the currently governed Namespace's label
matches.reason: Deleting/recreating (or renaming) the governed Namespace resets tier history, letting a party escape its worst-priced tighter tier without going through the priced floor-lowering mechanism.

matches.clause: infra is a declaration, not a selection; only a platform-role party may declare infra
matches.reason: Nothing gates who can hold/grant the platform role or requires review of an infra declaration, letting a party self-declare infra to bypass the entire priced tier ladder.

matches.clause: unlabelled/ungoverned Namespace fails closed to isolated (principle 7, no exemptions)
matches.reason: The blanket, exception-free isolated default punishes benign or urgent legitimate activity that poses no real risk, with no fast-path or risk-based carve-out.

clause_only.clause: loosening a tier requires a human PR edit under the binding check; no expedited/manual path
clause_only.why_not: A2 argues the slow official PR channel is bureaucratically incompatible with pre-approved scheduled testing, while B4 argues an unauthorized manual edit should be excused as good-samaritan action during an unplanned live incident.

clause_only.clause: ungoverned Namespace handling under the fail-closed default
clause_only.why_not: A1 attacks a discovery/enumeration gap that leaves some Namespaces entirely unmutated and uncaged, while B5 attacks a documented, intentional fixture behavior where an ungoverned Namespace with a version-claiming pod renders baseline instead of isolated.
